lyrics.title: I want to see you
lyrics.body:
Another day in the house and my "being" is all bored;
i'll wear the same clothes, in the mirror tolike me.
I'll wake up in the routine and open the curtain,
i'll finish the book and listen to the bulletin.

‘I’ll text you. 
tell me about a movement;
but that's not enough, because...

 I want to see you. 

My head is spinning, the battery is getting discharged,
the silence, the first sound; the wall has meaning now!
I look at you in the picture, before they put the "crown" on us.
But I miss your voice, your "together" and "why".

And so I grab my guitar,
my pen and my longing,
just to tell you him;
this last verse,
my thinking to succeed,
since you are not here:

 I want to see you.

lyrics.title: Love Is
If I didn't have
lyrics.body:
If I didn't have these too, what would I do?
What would I be?
How would I speak to the world - the outside and the inside?
How would I tell it that it's defective, yet attractive;
that it's unfair, yet tolerable;
that it's big, but also small.

If I didn't have these too, what would I say?
How would I pass my nights
sleepless from the squall of thoughts;
How would I appreciate my days
lost in a game of words.
What would I listen to in those moments when the ego suffers crises?
when unanswered questions about life, about love, about the unattainable
warm my humble flesh
and melt it,
stripping bare the defenseless yet proud spirit.

If I didn't have these too, what would I look like?
The moment of creation isn't stored
like a memory;
it only exists, offers, and gets lost in the cynicism of the present.
And afterwards, nothing!
I wake from the lethargy of spiritual intensity and am transported
at astronomical speed
into the reality of my senses.
And the senses get back to work:
they gather life like a sponge
and when they overflow, they squeeze it all out onto the paper.

If I didn't have these too, how would I live?
I am the servant of my own art.
What does the meager body need to survive?
That's what I give it:
Food, water, and love.
I prolong life and existence, one moment at a time.
I live it to the fullest, because when the spirit stops asking,
then I will be liberated;
then I will live dryly and humanly;
then the body will serve nothing,
only its nature.
And its nature wants it dead.

If I didn't have these too, I would burst;
I would be fed up with the humble common life of society;
of this artifact of human-animal desire
to live until its time comes;
from natural causes - no sooner than it should.
As if this artifact doesn't kill it sooner.

If I didn't have these too, what would I leave behind?
my descendants;
my legacy;
my words.
Often combined in various ways:
sometimes in a silly way,
sometimes in a somewhat more refined way,
other times in a freer way.
Sometimes they bind me for days, months, years;
other times for minutes or hours.
They always come and find me.
I always wait for them, they never wait for me.
I'm never sure what births them;
not my choices, of that I'm sure.
They create my footprint;
my identity;
my ink.
I serve as a translator to the outside world.
It's not an easy job;
this world speaks many languages.
if I didn't have these too, I don't know.

If I didn't have my children, what would I care for?

If I didn't have my songs, then what?

lyrics.title: By Heart
lyrics.body:
God spreads a black veil
and the sky extinguishes
the light of the stars
around your face.

You lean slowly
against my shoulder
and tenderly,
a little timidly,
you sing to your own tune
your "I love you."

It is your voice, my sweet,
that pushes me to find
whatever my heart desires,
whatever it keeps hidden.

It is your two eyes
that keep me alive
within the spindles of time,
amidst this empty life.

It is your sweet kiss,
that haunts my mind,
that unlocks pieces
of my tender self.

It is your two lips,
that seal me in yesterday.
There where the sun forgets to rise,
there where the silences speak.

God spreads a black veil
and the sky extinguishes
the light of the stars
around your face.

You lean slowly
against my shoulder
and tenderly,
a little timidly,
you sing to your own tune
your "I love you."

lyrics.title: What It Wants
lyrics.body:
I ask interest-free for a loan,
not in money, but alone
a little emotion.

In this servile age of ours,
where they stand at attention for hours
for five work-stamps.

I ask for a conversation partner,
to speak without delay, harder
with honesty.

And not be like those who appear,
to whisper in your ear
obedient words.

I ask for an untamed soul
to get the 4x4 on a roll
for adventure,

and not from the couch, away
social media and a frappé,
arrogant jawline.

A free spirit I seek
and not even for a week
talk of commitment.

The world's conventional, high,
pointlessly submissive, why
to sterile inspiration.

In this desolate time,
whatever the soul asks to align
hardly ever comes.

I didn't try too hard, this path,
always a new kiss in the aftermath
will succeed it.

I don't want to admit state
that ever since I was eighteen
I've been searching for love.

And when I find it lounging about, no flaw,
I let a hundred labors thaw
to leave unyielding.

lyrics.title: It's not
lyrics.body:
It's not that in my mouth
my speech was locked
is that inside my body
My heart aches. 

It's not like my lips
they won't talk to you
is that they want more
kiss you again.

How you and I are asking me
can we just be friends?
You seem to forget that until yesterday
we kissed on the lips.
Don't touchme, don't laugh at me;
they take it elsewhere.
Don't look at me, don't talk to me;
words hurt me.

It's not like my eyes
they don't want to look for you
it's just that they can't
or have them look at you.

It's not that when they find you
don't recognize you
is how they realize
the mistake and weep

lyrics.title: You are there
lyrics.body:
You're there looking at me,
as you proudly looked at every step.
You're there to hug me,
not to get wet when the wave hit me.

You're there and I love you
even if I don't see you, let me not touch you;
that's why I hurt, that's why I bend.
HereI am, your grandson, continuing,
and where you carved I step on it and move on.
You're my grandmother, my hero, and I love you.

You're there when I laugh,
because those moments with you, they raised me.
You're there, if I break something,
because your lips never scolded me.

Are you there?

You're here and I'm talking to you,
a restless soul, resting.
And if I sing with tears,
it's Υiorgos, a small child, who still needs you.

lyrics.title: Out
lyrics.body:
This isn't going on the album,
it has no truths for you to believe.
It only carries the risk
of destroying the fairytale;
To return to all your fears
and fight everything you couldn't bear.

I have no voice, yet I curse;
I have no water, yet I thirst for mistakes.
Now I touch my body
and search for the passions of a child.
But I always hide,
I run and hide
in your embrace, just as you've taught me.
But I'm in my own world
and when I shatter,
I hide in the depths of my mind.

Maybe love is suffocating me,
maybe your love is redeeming me.
The vicious cycle doesn't end
and your opinion surrounds me;
and I feel alone, no side of me completes me;
and it's what's inside me that makes me angry.

This isn't going on the album,
now I've started to regret it.
I can't find the meaning anywhere;
that must be the reason I survive,
on an unknown road in the wrong key.
What I became, what I loved,
here I was born, here I end.

lyrics.title: In conclusion
lyrics.body:
To stay
two friends
you asked me
stubbornly
I refused

What would I do with your friendship?

It would only serve to remind me of your
kiss

Your kiss
with a
privative alpha
at its end

---

**Wordplay Explanation:**

In Greek, the word for "friendship" is **φιλία** (*filia*), while the word for "kiss" is **φιλί** (*fili*).

Additionally, the "privative alpha" (*στερητικό άλφα*) in Greek grammar is a prefix attached to words to denote absence or negation (equivalent to the English prefix "un-" or "a-", as in *amoral* or *asymmetrical*).

The author plays with these linguistic concepts to show that accepting "friendship" (**φιλία**) after a romantic relationship feels like taking away the "kiss" (**φιλί**) and replacing it with a lack or absence—turning a kiss into a form of deprivation.

lyrics.title: Love in defeatism
lyrics.body:
My soul I deposited with you
a victim of your love I fell
my heart I delivered to you
my ego I flattened

My life I lent to you
and the interest I forgave you
And even if I left you your space
Know that I loved you very much

But the grievance seizes me
of egoism the abundance

How did they change so easily
our calls on the phone?
How are the times measured
when she asks to be alone?

Emotional instability
Love in defeatism
Confusion and incoherence
Relief of debt from commitment

I insist on the effort

---

Unanswered questions
backward go the steps
victims of our expectations
like a battle with the waves

With honesty I spoke to you
on the forehead I kissed you
and goodbye I whispered to you
it hurt, but I didn't break

But the grievance seizes me
before I turn the block

How did they turn into problems
your own feelings
to what measure on what scale
and got erased from the board?

Emotional instability
Love in defeatism
Confusion and incoherence
Relief of debt from commitment

I continue the effort

---

You were seen with a stranger
infidelity's mystery
the paradox of your silence
signifying an inglorious end

I will pick up my pieces
I will dry my eyes too
engraved are my marks
in my heart now empty

But the grievance seizes me
And has left me speechless

How did they dry up so fast
your heart's comforting
touches, kissing, messages
the signs of your love

Emotional instability
Love in defeatism
Confusion and incoherence
Relief of debt from commitment

I stop the effort
So many errors, so much ignorance

lyrics.title: Prison
lyrics.body:
Your mind is a prison,
that stays open at night.
When you step out of your cells, don't forget your glasses,
because by the time you return, morning will have come.

You say you can't take it here anymore
yet you do nothing about it.
You instantly push the button to run the box,
just to supposedly escape anxiety's fever.

Your life has hypothermia, but you don't want a doctor
and don't search for your symptoms on your phone;
search within yourself, swim to the depths of your soul
and tell your fear: "I'm afraid I won't be afraid of you."
Are you sure you want to be hospitalized?
Stay strong, don't become easy prey for the predators;
you have the spirit as your weapon, your soul as your shield;
remember, what meaning will you give to your life.
Your house is small and your fridge is old,
the shelf is broken, the landscape blurry.
And you whine, always wanting, wanting, wanting more.
Do you want a life like this? Tell me what you truly want.
Fake-culture for rent at retail prices;
fads that come and go, void of logic;
pseudo-quality and puffed-up, big words;
a life built on lies, why do you want it? I've got more to tell you.

Every passing day feels like I'm in a prison
and what truly terrifies me
is that in this prison the door is open,
I can leave whenever I want, but the outside terrifies me
and I don't want to leave.
I want to get out before it's too late and the door shuts
and I live forever in cells;
the times don't help,
they want me locked inside with my mouth shut,
laughing, rejoicing, and saying thank you
for being a convict in this fake life.
I want to live a life that is distinct;
when I leave, to still be remembered,
as the one who had no mouth
who had a tommy gun and shot anyone standing in front.
The street is the truth, that's why we stay on the street,
we don't forget those gone because of a foolish cop
and for those who left, and those who will leave along the way;
I can't imagine having to hold your funeral.
You say you can't take it here anymore;
look at me boiling tonight, boiling tonight with fever.
I want to throw up what's inside me, like vomiting,
to disgust passersby so they see what I mean.
When I say I want to get out of here, I want to get out of here;
to burn down the brothel, leaving only concrete.
I want to get out of here, I want to get out of here
to burn down the brothel, leaving only concrete.

No one is ever wrong about anything;
everyone shouts out loud, defending the unsaid.
Ears are open, but they don't listen;
and if something goes wrong, everyone demands explanations.
I'm disgusted by this society you want,
it thinks it's moving forward, but it's returning to yesterday.
I'm tired of satisfying my pride,
I have no price tag, my soul is not for sale.
Shame on me, I owe my existence to this art;
I have every syllable of mine as my family;
every verse I birth is my child,
whenever I break out of routine's underground prison.

Your mind is a prison,
that stays open at night.
When you step out of your cell, throw away your key somewhere,
that's how you'll know you're doing the right thing.

You say you can't take it here anymore,
now you're doing something about it;
you instantly push the button, to enjoy the moment
of a carefree relationship with your true self.

lyrics.title: Summer Rain
lyrics.body:
First rains wet my heart again
and I dance the festive ones in the sky.
I'm waiting for you to come back to me
and take my joy away.

I always feast as a monk, a monk
and I'm not complaining.
But how I want your hug, how
summers when the alleys are wet!

Winters no longer work for me;
i can't stand the weather.
Summer, but hands frozen;
i go out to burn in the rain.

I always party alone, I always party alone...

Since everything in the world is planned,
let me stand before fate.
With my eyes dull, in love,
yours, even if I die, so that I may see.

I always party alone, I always party alone...

lyrics.title: Kamara
lyrics.body:
You're late and I'm waiting,
on the bench I'm looking at the arch.
I see anxiety spread everywhere,
some gentlemen are talking about the metro.

And everyone is going, going somewhere;
to everywhere and to nothing and returning back.
Pigeons flying,
where could the hope be that they're searching to find?

I'm waiting and breathing
the minutes that away from you I'll have to live.
And I keep going, but where am I going?
I've left but again here I'll return
to wait for you.

Hurried drivers are waiting for the traffic light;
Navarinou is filling up with people.
Two boys manage to catch a kiss,
before the exhaust fumes smell like mint.

And everyone is going, going somewhere...

lyrics.title: Love Anthology: A
lyrics.body:
Night had just fallen
On the beach -
On our beach -
Where we first kissed
Lying on the sand
Silence all around, stillness
Us silent
You broke your silence
With a complaint
"when will he write something for me", you answered back

"I've told you, my beloved, that lyrics
Come to me suddenly and by chance," I replied to you

You smiled slightly.
Two or three jokes followed.
Pointless.

An elaborate maneuver.

Bypassed. Perhaps
forgotten.
But I didn't forget.
So I wrote to you...

Just as the wave crashes softly on the coastline
and as the step finds its rhythm in the music
So my heart rhythmically
for you alone will beat
That night

The last night of April
With the sunrise
Grillis and Saint George's day
Would be succeeded by the last month of Spring
May
May
With its wreath
With its struggles
With its Blossoms

Source of inspiration

You thought I forgot
But I didn't forget
So I wrote to you...

Just as May always follows April
and as the earth revolves around the Sun
So my body will wander
to find you whom it seeks

lyrics.title: Love Anthology: Z
lyrics.body:
Daylight would break in a short while
How did time pass like that?
Time flows fast with you
I don't know if we said all we wanted to say
As much again wouldn't be enough
One last embrace
And off we went
Just enough to catch the reflection of
Venus

Intoxicating, the colors

You thought I forgot.
But I didn't forget.
So I wrote to you...

Just as Uranus embraces Gaia
and as the morning star emerges momentarily
To find myself in your embrace
for a moment, even if I get lost

July
The next day I was leaving
Days it would take for me to see you
Would you miss me?
Who knows?
Rhetorical, the questions
One last kiss
for goodbye
Not for goodbye
for a safe journey
The distance will not wear us down
and this waiting will boost
the passion
The passion for reconnection
and the desire for one more kiss

Redeeming, the return

You believed I forgot.
But I didn't forget.
So I wrote to you...

Just as he still yearns for Ithaca
and as Odysseus kisses her soil
So with yearning I desire
to taste your two lips

It's been a long time
since our last kiss

Not even the taste of your lips anymore
can I remember

Since our last meeting
it's been a long time
How much time has passed
indefinite

Neither the how nor the who
can I answer
they do not help
my mind and my heart

evasive objectors

The only certain thing is the pain
in every effort to recall you
in my memory

You believed I forgot.
I didn't forget you.
And yet I lost you...

I had hidden from you, my beloved, that lyrics—
and if they arise suddenly and by chance—
are mainly a distillation of pain
both a curse and a privilege of the lonely one.

lyrics.title: MICROCOSMOS ft. Nicolas Sosa
lyrics.body:
I've got our bags packed and ready,
we don't need much,
just motivation.
There are some beautiful islands,
you can see the Mediterranean
from our balcony.

Give me a place in your heart,
so I can taste the intoxication
of your kisses tonight.
Beers beneath the moon
and our minds will set sail,
as we say "I love you."

I want to kiss you following this flow
I want to taste your salt under the sun

You'll be a Latin melody,
a familiar harmony
to an exotic rhythm.
I'll be a ship at the bottom of your sea,
upon your salty neck
I'll be lost forever.

Blessed be that Italian girl
who makes the landscape
look spectacular.
I've already lost all the bets,
there's no clothing left on me
that I could possibly wager.

I want to kiss you following this flow
I want to taste your salt under the sun

Fogging up the lenses of your glasses,
Thelma and Louise, with no signal.
Tie me up with your sarong,
and if it comes undone, no one saw a thing.

No one else will see this dream,
only the stars, only us

I want to kiss you following this flow
I want to taste your salt under the sun

lyrics.title: Ninemia
lyrics.body:
A broken boat with oars
stretches far across the open seas,
seeking to escape.

In the heart of the wind it roams
and the wave misleads it
and wraps around it.

It washes ashore on an unknown coast,
dizzy from the saltiness.
Its timber frames are bent,
betrayed by fate.

In your deep eyes, my love, I'll find
the lost tranquility.
My homeland is all the water,
yet my Ithaca is one.

A broken boat with oars,
that has the wind as a companion
commanding its course.

It fears not going out to the open sea,
longing for home carries sacred charms
for its stronghold.

It washes ashore on an unknown coast(...)

A broken boat with oars
is now at Aeolus's mercy
and sails on.

It rises amidst the darkness,
it has changed color in its sails
and sets..

lyrics.title: Rethymno
lyrics.body:
Like the sea merging with the stars
is you and me, a few empty summers.
Your land is an island, the wave caresses it;
my journey is you, seeking your soil.

And Rethymno awakens to bring love,
in a passion that begs for just a little more summer...

I kissed your gaze with the lips of my eyes,
I tasted a sweet August dusk.
"A little blue, a lot of water," you told me your secret;
was your hand cool, or was it your smile?

And Rethymno awakens to bring love,
in a passion that begs for just a little more summer...

Tonight I'll come to your shore on a boat,
my map is a canvas, my compass your body.
What worth is life without a touch of madness;
how sweet life is, seen through a girl's eyes!

And Rethymno awakens to bring love,
in a passion that begs for just a little more summer...

lyrics.title: Reggae Ballada
lyrics.body:
A thousand miles of road, I waited for you but you were late
and two kisses at the door, when you left you gave.
You entered my life and yet you turned to dust
and everything that reminds me of you now kills me.

And right where I said twice again I would betray
everything and yield to your lips once more,
you told me you'd have me in your heart forever;
that's why I wrote a reggae ballad for you.

I know, like a fairytale it all seems now;
and our love like an endless storm,
like a fairytale with no end and no beginning;
but you, my heart, were not there.

In other songs you stare at the lyrics,
with your guitar you steal loves,
you give and take, selling notes;
just like the dreams that shattered for us.

You laid me down, looked at me, the shirt gets in the way
and your neck, strongly, smells of lavender.
You smiled at me, embraced me, were checking the time;
your body in my hand shouts "go ahead."

"Go ahead, to feel what nightmare means"
and you slipped into my sheets like a stowaway.
You gave me, put on me a gold ring;
I need to understand this game of yours.

I know...

Scissors; my dreams went to the side,
when your eyes were pouring a river of tears.
I covered your eyelids with my fingers,
wiped you clean and showed you that you're mine.

My little one, hear a piece of good advice from me:
"grab hold of your dreams and don't stay with me."
I wish the kilometers were made of cardboard,
we'd be carriages on the same train again.

I know...

And yet, you fly far away and I
like a fool count the days.
You come, you go, the same old thing again;
I'm tired now, my loneliness hunts me down.

I miss you, you know it, after all this time;
who knows what I'd do to have you here!
I miss your eyes, I miss your voice,
calling out "leave" while I was right there with you.

My days empty, my nights endless;
I remember when you lived here yet were absent.
I understand now what you meant to me,
but I let you go and everything is lost.

I'm in pain, I hesitate, I tremble at the thought
of your lips kissing somewhere else.
But I know that when I look into your eyes,
they tell me truths without speaking.

I know...

I'll remember you, know that forever,
and I gift you this reggae ballad;
like two songs that became one again,
so what if in truth everything remained broken!

A thousand words wander inside my head,
but how will you bear what I want to tell you!
It's not hard, close your eyes...

I love you so much.

lyrics.title: Peach
lyrics.body:
I'm searching to find what we have in common
with our bicycle.
Could it be the little bell
you ring so I'll come out to the alley?

Could it be the old handlebars,
though with so many turns, even they won't straighten out?
Then maybe it's the brake,
but that's been broken for so many years too.

If it's not the old handlebars,
nor the brake, nor the little bell,
what we have in common is right on the wheel—
our squashed little peach (ro-daki-no).

lyrics.title: On a finish background
lyrics.body:
I changed
my phone wallpaper out of
a need
to protect myself
every time the phone rings
or a message comes in
and it isn't you

We will no longer be
the two of us in an embrace
the first image I see
when I wake up
in the morning

I chose
from the suggested wallpapers
at random
hastily
a wavy sea
with a sun
rosy-red
in the background

Unsuccessfully
I would say
since my thoughts
start from
you again and to
you
they lead

And my mind goes
as I face the sea
to the so many waves
of our shared
path
the hardships of life that together
we leaped over and
until today
we had coexisted
well

And to the
deep dives
my mind goes
that you took
all by yourself with a
snorkel and
a mask
exploring the unknown
the deep dives that
you wanted so much
for us to take together
and I was afraid to follow
making excuses that
I had just eaten and that
I had a heavy stomach or that
I was tired

* I was a coward and
Fear possessed me, but,
I didn't want to show you -

If only time
would turn back and
I would plunge into the water with you for hours

---

And this
sunset
in the background
instantly breeds a reasonable question in me
is the sun rising, or is it setting?

And suddenly this question becomes
the spring
of an innermost thought that
the sunset ultimately symbolizes
the endless cycle of life
within which
everything that begins
is led
at some point
inevitably
to the end

And just as
intoxicating
the beginning is
equally
intoxicating
the end must be too
which always marks
a new beginning
longed for
even if it hurts
even if it darkens
our life
for a short while

Now
that clearly
I can see
things
having distilled well
the pain you
caused me
with the
unexpected and abrupt
ending of
our relationship

Now I can
consciously
declare
that you entered my life during a period
of darkness
and you illuminated it
you gave it meaning
you gave it motivation
you pushed it forward
and like a breakwater you shielded it
to withstand the
blows

And when you fulfilled your role
and there was nothing left for you
to offer it
bravely you decided to
set

So with gratitude I bid you farewell,
even though I was hurt.

Wounds have their own
meaning too

they guide you through life
they offer you
precious lessons

they mark you
unabashedly
so that your soul too
-when you reach the end-
has proof and
evidence
that it lived

And if in the end
many questions
remained unanswered
just a single question answered in the affirmative would
bring me peace:

that my own
sun
for you
at its setting and in your darkness
carved something good in
your soul

Only gratitude
remains
without any
hope
for a return

And yet it would be
selfish
to rule out the possibility
that perhaps one day
our paths will cross again
and our stars will align
reserving
for each other
a new
Sunrise.

lyrics.title: Hyperbole
lyrics.body:
Another day
-one of the few, to tell the truth,
yet getting more and more frequent-
where we won't have exchanged a word
-not a sweet and tender one
like once upon a time
in that earlier season-
just a simple word

Where the phone won't have rung
not even once
with you on the other end
asking me how I am
-how I feel, that is, and how I spent today;
I want so badly to hope that
at least for now
you haven't yet forgotten my
face-

Where you won't have sent
an old photo of ours
in a text message
-you used to do that once;
That's how you declared your "presence"
and your "I'm thinking of you"
"I'm thinking of US"

"I love you."

And somehow like this evening will fall
and another night will have arrived
-one of the frequent ones, to tell the truth,
and getting more and more numerous lately-
where I will lie down
by myself on the
floor
flat on my back
-not on the double mattress;
on the floor.
The mattress is too big and doesn't
suit
my loneliness-

Where I'll be staring at the ceiling
And the chandelier
-not the stars on a beach by the waves
like we used to-

Where I'll be listening only to my silence
-I won't have any thoughts to make;
Better that way! They torment me so much lately-

And I'll hear the footsteps
of the dog
belonging to the neighbor on the second floor

-he at least made peace with his solitude
and chose
the only certain
loyal friend to make it
tolerable-

Midnight.
And early tomorrow morning the wake-up call

Before I fall asleep
if I make the decision to call first myself
you'll probably have it turned off
pretending it ran out of battery.

But if I'm lucky and you pick up
then I'll come face to face with a
sorrowful
coldness
-frequent, very frequent, lately-
a feeling expressed, perhaps
in the most authentic way
and sterilized
of any displays of passion you used to have.

And if this
complaint of mine
we end up discussing
then you'll tell me that I'm exaggerating

So be it.
Let me be exaggerating.
That is a good sign of love
which happens to be (as it should)
the source of my exaggeration
and of the cunning thought (of fear)
that your own love has run dry.

And what, then, wouldn't I give for you to
exaggerate
too, once again
for a little while
I would rejoice in it so much.

Perhaps then
I wouldn't have any complaint to hold against you.

lyrics.title: The meaning of life
lyrics.body:
So many years the same joke: the same face in the morning,
same pencil on paper, same line in the book.
So many months the same phrase: "I've had enough by now,"
not a single change; I think I've truly lost my mind!

Give meaning to my life,
take me out of my prison,
hide in the dream with me,
live in another era.

Give a reason to live,
burst out, get out of here,
reach where you shouldn't go;
a life is waiting for you.

So many hours I've been waiting with a coral suitcase,
same color since I was a child; but the train is late, I see.
I don't care where I go, I leave the suitcase, I run
and I can't stand the phonies; same world, I'm forgetting you.

Give meaning to my life...

Same love you love, same friend you kiss,
same table in the kitchen you wait to eat at.
Same words at school: "put something on, it's cold,"
same idea you carry: "same world, where are you taking me?".

Give meaning to my life...

This is the meaning of life.

lyrics.title: I'm sinking
lyrics.body:
I'm sinking
and getting addicted
to an endless winter of the mind.

I'm sinking
and losing hope
I turn off the lights and my thoughts drift away.

I fall again like rain into the void
and my endurance is like a drizzle in the ocean;
and I'm sinking..

I'm sinking
and tuning in
to the frequencies of a barren life.

I'm sinking
and getting disarmed
I get rid of the servants of pleasure.

I fall again like rain into the void...

lyrics.title: Breakup
lyrics.body:
Fiery tears; rain falling.
A love that bleeds.
Mournful colors of the mind;
shades of a clouded sky.

A strong gust of anger
extinguishes love's light.
And love's fragile thread—
it takes just a single word to break it.

Ego flares up.
Heartbreak lies in wait.
Only a sense of obsession remains,
without a drop of patience.

Life's solemn glory,
merely a moment's power.
Countless loves on wings
flying everywhere and nowhere.

writings.title: Overflow
writings.body:
I have written before about the small plant I have in my student home;
well remember, the one that only needs a little water and light to bloom.
But the problem is that it needs some water.
How can this be a problem?
Each time, I water it before its time because I can't wait to water it.
Every time, I give him more than he asks for.
Each time the pot plate overflows and I wipe the furniture with paper.

When we love someone, we often give them more than they ask for and can handle.
So I remember from now on, giving his soil time to absorb the water I give him.

There is a price to be paid for loving;
(but between us, love and let the saucer overflow; there will be someone who will accept all your water)

85 — m

writings.title: Wireless headphones
writings.body:
You wake up one day, and,
as usual,
you wear your wireless headphones
and you choose the repertoire of the day.
Your headphone case is located
in your open right pocket.
You get on the subway,
you arrive at your destination,
you make a move to put the headphones back in their case,
the case of your headphones is not located
in your open right pocket.
Your headphone case is not on you.
Your headphones will “live” until their battery runs out •
you accept it.
What repertoire will you listen to now?
P.S. Listen to this repertoire.
85 — m

writings.title: Assad means happy
writings.body:
Assad is 24 years old, from Syria. He comes from a family with 9 other siblings.
He is married and has a one-year-old child. Due to the civil war happening in his country, he saw one of his brothers forced to kill another brother of his.
"I didn't want to kill anyone" and in 2015 (at 15 years old) he left for Istanbul.
"I couldn't find work in Turkey, there is a lot of racism. I couldn't feed my family" and, last October, he got on a boat in the Sea of Marmara and crossed over to the island of Leros (illegally, he said), for €6,000. His wife and child stayed behind.
Since February he has been working in Athens, at a textile factory.
He hasn't seen his parents and siblings for 10 years.
-Is Syria beautiful, Assad?
-Very. Until they destroyed it.
For 4 hours we were sitting next to each other on the train and hadn't exchanged a word. Until, with immense politeness and a smile, he asked me "Athens?" pointing at his watch. I told him in English "we are arriving now in an hour." He didn't understand. Because he didn't know a single word of English. And for the remaining hour we had a unique conversation through sign language and Google Translate. Him in Arabic, me in Greek.
Assad wasn't educated, he left school so he wouldn't die. And yet he is a dignified man, smiling.
However
Assad is not happy or content.
-It was my honor to meet you. You are good.
-The honor is mine, Assad.

y.f.

writings.title: Walk on the 25th of August
writings.body:
The center of Heraklion consists of two cities that coexist
each in its own time:
the one at eye level •
and fromher when you look up.

writings.title: Dialogue
writings.body:
-Ilove you very much
-Ilove you very much
Have a good time. 
-Have fun
-Thanks
-Good jobaa
-Thank you very much
-Very good jobaaaa
-Thanks
-Please, Ilove you very much
-And I

What if there are problems,
what if we live under pressure.
Love always cheers us up.
and this morning's funny dialogue of the neighbors daddy - little daughter made my day.

"When life leaves us blind
love keeps us kind"
The Messenger, Linkin Park

85 — m

writings.title: Chapels
writings.body:
A deeply hidden memory came to me today, as I was driving on VOAK from Heraklion towards Rethymno:
I was no more than 5 years old, in the car with my grandfather
and we had set a challenge for the trip:
to make the sign of the cross whenever I saw a church or roadside shrine.
We were laughing at how good I was at it,
and how I picked up on all of them, even the ones hidden behind bushes,
even though they were truly SO many.
My joy with this game was immense,
I had a wonderful time that day.
Today, as I came across those endless shrines on the roadside again,
hidden behind bushes,
the feeling was completely different
because now I am grown up and driving
and I know.

y.f.

writings.title: One
writings.body:
A moment of solitude on the balcony of a house in a village near Sitia, where nothing but natural sounds could be heard, was enough to make me realize that I have gloriously taken part in an eternal, global feast.

Facing me on an electric pole, I observe a gecko silently, patiently, and with total focus stalking behind an unidentified insect that is heading upward, likely searching for its evening meal, while simultaneously feeling under a persistent raid of mosquitoes and gnats continuously targeting my sweet blood, which I had just charged with the sugar of the fruit drink that happened to be in the fridge, at the exact same time I'm trying to peel a firiki apple I found on the kitchen counter—and eventually abandoned because I noticed a hole from a little worm that had obviously discovered it before me.

And that is how fellow-feeders [syn-trofoi] the imperfect creation moves. Always chasing after something you lack and the other possesses. And this happens within the bounds of an endless futility, which makes me wonder: if we were indeed One, would we find our completeness and thereby escape the pain of need? Or does this condition prove beyond a doubt that everything is One?
And I speak of the Uni-verse [Syn-pan].

y.f.

writings.title: Flame
writings.body:
It always catches me writing when I travel. Mostly airplanes, I don't know. Maybe because this high flying takes me out of my box: like I'm getting air. Today I did not know why I took out the pad to write, I always carry it with me but I rarely use it. Like I'm afraid that when this damn inspiration comes, I won't have paper to turn it into words. It's like everything revolves around her. Who's she? I don't know how to answer. The One of Phoebus perhaps: that is everything, always and everywhere; that you love, claim, sacrifice yourself for her and in the end you are killed. And then, like another Prometheus, you are born again and she eats your livers again, thus punishing you for the sin of taking the flame from God and sharing it. You make the inexplicable and unpredictable divine, casual. And then it eats your liver. Intensity. Heart.
I don't know who you are, while you only saw someone named Giorgos give you a piece of paper from a pad that talks about arson and miracles. Flame. Intensity. That's what came to mind when we looked at each other. You didn't speak. Tension. But you gave me a sweet smile, like you said "thank you for your paper, although I don't know yet what it contains". Tension. I lost my posture. Syntagma took me.
Now I sit tied up and compose in a rusty PPC box, humanizing the divine. Like another eagle, it will eat my livers. Then I'll be reborn. But the Metro will be gone by now.
Intencity
like another eagle, I just woke up flying over burning and flooded Athens•
ina tight plane.
85 — m

writings.title: Light
writings.body:
In a process of renewing my student apartment, 
i thought it would be appropriate to add a little “nature” to the space,
buying a plant. 

I enter the first flower shop I find in front of me:
- Hi, I'd like a pot with an indoor plant to decorate. 
It took a while for the florist to show me all my options,
explaining to me in detail the needs of each plant. 

-This one looks beautiful. I think I'll take this.
-Perfect, let me inform you that you should have this in a bright spot of the house, otherwise it will wither. It blooms winter - summer, however it has this peculiarity. 

And yes, that was where I realized I was going to buy something that has life. 
-But where I want to put it, there's not much light.
-What can I tell you, do you want to go to a cactus? Or risk it? 

I risked it. And you know why? Our soul often only asks for Light. Otherwise it will wither.
We, everyday life, society, obligations
we insist on placing it in dark places for show, 
disregarding its living side.
So I decided not to go to a cactus•
not to choose the easy solution. 

Because I decided to take care of my Soul
like the plant:
to have her permanently exposed to the Light.

85 — m

writings.title: Vacuum cleaner
writings.body:
An ordinary, student day.
The morning awakening - albeit brutal - motivated me to organize the rest of my day. So I decide, after an "educational" obligation, to clean the house.
I arrange my things and clothes, I wash some dishes that were left over from last night, I do the laundry, I go to the supermarket for two or three things that I was missing, I clean my guitars, I dust. Too much work already, and I hadn't even picked up the vacuum cleaner.
It's her time.
She waited patiently for me in her place - placed in a strange, crooked position because my apartment is not famous for its spaciousness...
I pull the cord, plug it in. Suddenly, without any recent similar experience, it catches up with me and I start to sneeze nonstop. And again. And again. To the point where I got tired and left the broom as it was and sat down to calm down.
I usually get such allergies, but not so abruptly!
Having calmed down, I go back to work and notice that the broom is full of dust! I realize that I had dusted every aspect of the house except the broom itself; and of course this little detail wasted part of my strength, after causing me an inexplicable, unstoppable sneeze.
We all know that the role of the vacuum cleaner is to sweep. To clean. To bind all the waste material that covers the floor, including dust.
But it is not a given that the vacuum cleaner itself is clean, wiped clean!

Many times, we are so “crazy” about our roles; 
with our obligations to the environment• 
with the rules• 
that we forget to take care of ourselves. 
We forget to “wipe” ourselves from the “dust” we bind from others.

We forget to give ourselves time and space;
rest him body and soul;
nourish and water it properly;
wash it properly;
to love him. 
Because when we don't, then we lose our energy from the reflex "sneeze" that tells us:
'WHOA, YOU'RE DOING SOMETHING WRONG, BROTHER.'
Wipe your broom often.

85 — m

writings.title: Coffee
writings.body:
I like to go
in a corner Turkish cafe,
where Turks work.
Typically, what I order is:
a kunefe (they do it brilliantly)
and coffee which, logically, holds a record with the most names in the world•
the well-known Greek, Turkish, Armenian, Cypriot, Asia Minor.
Obviously, the name is specified
by the people who drink it
and as we know,
everything ethnic that is, in its essence, common
raises controversy.
What would you want?
Wanting to be discreet and not "provocative", I reply:
'I'd like a kunefe and a medium Turkish coffee.'
'You mean Greek?'
Surprised, I say "Yes!".
Love the essence,
accepting the different,
may THE neighbor's goat live.
That's respect.
85 — m

writings.title: Captain Michalis
writings.body:
Listening to Hadjidakis' album
"Captain Michalis"
on the bus,
while, at the same time, out of my headphones
the voices are the protagonists
of my young Turkish fellow passengers,
who converse with laughter.

Kazantzakis' reality would not be far off.
Neither did that of Captain Michalis.

I smiled. The world is changing, Kemal.
85 — m

writings.title: Details
writings.body:
(...)
-Nice nice, your name?
-Yiannis.
-Yiannis?
-Yes yes.
-Alright Costa, talk to you later!
I had the luck of hearing this dialogue. Just now.
That's all.

y.f.

writings.title: Mousafiris
writings.body:
It was a flower:
my grandmother called it "mousafiri"•
that is, a guest.
Because, witha gentle breeze he scattered
-had sensitive shackles-
and requested hosting
where the wind traveled it.
On Grandpa's paddle,
in grandma's canyon,
in the lake of freshly watered apricot•
dismembered, but co-existing with the intact nature.

For my grandmother, all people 
they were musaphirs.

writings.title: The man wearing a violin
writings.body:
Warm winter morning in Thessaloniki
-what could be more usual, one might say-
crossing the threshold of the front door,
I began heading toward a musical instrument store.
At that exact moment, a gentleman carrying a violin passes right in front of me.
We were moving along the same street, so that it looked as if I were following him.
At some point he paused to look at the display window of a perfumery;
I passed him.
Not wanting to walk through the outdoor patio of a café, I chose a narrower sidewalk, where I had to wait because two elderly ladies were coming from the opposite direction.
He chooses the café patio;
he passed me.
At the pedestrian traffic light, we stood side by side.
Crossing it, I turned right, he kept straight.
Long story short, when I arrived, we ended up, out of courtesy, with him opening the door of the store for me, walking in right after me.
I was trying out guitars;
he asked about a bow.
That's somewhat how we interact with people in our lives:
we start from different places,
we walk in parallel,
we pass, we are passed by -each with a different Rhythm-
we wait together,
we choose different paths,
and in the end, we arrive at the Final Destination that we all know from the beginning
each devoted to their own passions
(and Passions).

y.f.

writings.title: Dreams
writings.body:
Last night
i dreamt of well-groomed girls,
well-dressed men,
flooding a fantastic street, my own, full of bars and restaurants.
There was no place to go through this torrent of youth, energy and excitement.
Everyone was naked;
from the neck upwards.
Beautiful.
It seemed to me a familiar image and at the same time so far away.

A Freudian would say that I made a journey into my innermost thoughts and desires, that I imagined what I cannot live.
That I want what I don't have, badly.

I woke up happy
because I took a walk in the paradise of our time
and I came back.
And I have to tell you, freedom is very sweet.
and it looks like fire. 

85 — m

writings.title: Visual
writings.body:
I woke up this morning 
with Nirvana's nevermind record
and in the last 10 minutesI have seen
4 people wearing Nirvana T-shirts.
That they weren't wearing any before?

We see in others
what we already have in mind.

Perhaps the recipe for managing interpersonal issues
is based on seeing others as they are
and not as we have them in our minds.
Nevermind.

85 — m

writings.title: Passion
writings.body:
I love hearing people speak passionately 
for their science - art. 

Whatever.

writings.title: The moment
writings.body:
Thoughts are confused,
the floor fluid,
the ceiling expands•
and I, moment in time and space,
i write about the futile,
for the written,
for the inevitable
... the moment is over!

writings.title: Parasites
writings.body:
A Sunday so full and stressful, 
a life around so calm and predictable; all in the schedule, all in the plan.
I pick up the package from the university club and sit on a bench to eat in peace before my busy day begins.

First I bring out the bread•
my bread falls down.
everywhere birds out of nowhere, all of a sudden, trying to squeeze out every crumb there is.

Second, I present the main meal•
everywhere cats out of nowhere, all of a sudden, staring at me with this fixation that says "give me."

Last I bring up the water bottle I had•
yes, there were wasps.

It reminded me of the people who aren't there for you but when you have something they need,
they appear out of nowhere, suddenly, demanding a piece of your food. And you give it all to them. Even if you're hungry.

A Sunday so full and stressful, 
a life around so calm and predictable; all in the schedule, all in the plan.

writings.title: Peeler
writings.body:
5 days ago I was peeling potatoes with the peeler.
I hit a hard potato,
i made a sudden move,
i created a deep cut on my thumb.
It was not so much the pain as the discomfort from the blood that flowed unceasingly.
The unstoppable continued for the next few days, 
because something would always be found to "disturb" the naked wound.

Today I was peeling potatoes with the peeler.
All normal, until I stood for quite some time, when I noticed
my wounded thumb facing the peeler,
‘As near as dammit, we do. 
and reminded me of when I'm standing across
and I look straight in the face
my executioners: my problems and fears.

I kept peeling potatoes with the peeler.

85 — m

writings.title: about waves
writings.body:
Pain moves at the speed of sound. In the detonation of the psyche, initially an impressive light is mapped out, traveling rapidly through space. Correspondingly, the entity of sound requires a longer duration to reach your ears. Especially if you are far from the detonation, it is at such a distance from the visual spectacle that it might even startle you, as you don't expect it.
and boom

y.f.

writings.title: Bicycle without wheels
writings.body:
I play basketball on a neighborhood court.
Everywhere around children
others playing chase,
other basketball, soccer,

a little boy with his dad is trying to learn how to ride a bike without wheels.

He comes in front of me and stops,
just before I shoot a good shot,
he lifts his head as if looking at a giant
and he says to me, with extra spontaneity:
-Sir, do you play for the national team?
-(laughing) No.
-Ah, because you are very good!!
-Thank you! I used to play in a team.
-What team?
-In Crete, it is..
-Well done, Ireally like this team!

and starts the bike.

The children are kind. They do not want to learn about degrees, distinctions, statistics and unnecessary fanfare. They don't want anything in return for a good word.
They won't ask anything they don't care about•
they will not continue a conversation because "it is uncomfortable not to talk when you are with someone".

Because children are real!
(and tsachpinika)

85 — m

writings.title: Pinch
writings.body:
You're handsome. You look good with a mustache. You seem like a nice guy.
Going to the bus station, huh?
Where are you going? Kavala? Larissa?
- I'm going to pick up a package.

Take care, my boy, God bless you.
Do you know where I'm going?
OSCAR CHEAL:  Where?

I'm going to do some dope. 
and his eyes burst, his voice trembled, his face was disfigured.

I'm in a lot of pain, my boy. I don't have a mom, I don't have a dad, they died in my arms.
I'm in trouble. How did I get in trouble like this?
I don't have a family, my wife divorced me, my children don't want me.
What am I doing? I'm in a lot of pain, my boy. If I start telling you the story of my life, you'll cry.
and the more I gave him space, the more he talked.

I'm looking to get high, that's where he got me.
I don't have anyone to tell. It hurts, boy. Take care of yourself, my boy. God bless you. 
and got off at the next stop.

I'm in pain with him. He didn't ask me for anything, not money, not to sell me, not to harass me.
Just a little time and a hug in his pain. Even though he had all the stereotypical external characteristics of a cruel migrant criminal.

I saw a small child in this cruel migrant criminal
crying out for love and understanding.

What do you see, where you look?

85 — m

writings.title: Morning flight
writings.body:
Night bus on the way to the airport.
I hold things and that's why I choose to sit all the way back. 
Opposite me sits only a woman who is worn out, tired, ragged. He writes something passionately, he notes something.
I open to read my book in case it gets a little late.

A man comes in, knew her from somewhere and greeted her:
- Are you okay? he asks with a smile.
-Tired, Nikos. Seven takes you left, don't push it.
- I'm not afraid of you.
-Seven takes you left. Don't push it. Repeat singing.

This is how my day began, early on, with this verse of Kavvadias from that lady.
I won't look behindthis. Seven takes me left, I don't push it. The one with the power.

P.S. Son, where are you going? 
mother I go to the airplanes

85 — m

writings.title: Get up.
writings.body:
Tough day, full of running, exams, setbacks..
In my haste upstairs, trying to manage to fulfill all my obligations, within the time frame set by law (I wonder how I say this and at the same time I do not live in 1970), 
with a rapid gait, subjected to the tyranny of the mask, with headphones and a loaded backpack, I cross Filippou on my way to Aristotelous Square.
My step is steadily fast, my gaze is fixed forward, my mind is creating the plan for the best possible management of the remaining time and the headphones there, to distract me from every sound dissonance of the city.

Passing by an old lady sitting in a chair, alone outside one of the many furniture stores of this particular street, I feel an attraction. 
I stop, take off my headphones and turn my eyes to the lady who was asking for my help.
'My lad, God bless you, help me up.'

I must admit, I was baffled.
It took a few tenths of a second for my mind to work out whether it was RIGHT to shake hands with this helpless lady and help her get back on her feet.
1. Doesn't he wear a mask?
2. Am I a random stranger and she asks me to touch her?
3. But isn't she afraid of having coronavirus, me the careless young man, and catching it? Vulnerable group is..
4. Did he really ask me, or does he have a problem? What are you getting into right now...

I give her my hands and some of my strength.
It hurt as she got up, but she finally got up. Who knows how long he waited for this moment.

The lady was not afraid of the coronavirus.
The lady was not afraid of me, the foreign, infectious and dangerous young man.
The lady asked for something very simple:
to get up.

Get up. 

85 — m

writings.title: Aside
writings.body:
I am moved when sequence and order
and the irritations
and the routine of the street
step aside
(literally)
at the sound of an ambulance siren.
Suddenly you see everyone acquiring
a common goal:
to put aside their hurry,
their Ego
and cooperate,
forming a chaos
of disorganized
and unaligned vehicles;
"Of course even this chaos
arises from a law"
someone would say.
Perhaps I am moved that it arises
from something deeper:
from an inner Law
that has the power to put the law
aside.

y.f.

writings.title: In the same head
writings.body:
Going down to the Rotunda,
i have usurumin my headphones.

In the three minutes I was introducing myself to a part of them I didn't know
my gaze catches a street sweeper
who whistled-even though I didn't hear him.

At the exact same moment, he reached the point in the song
where the singer whistles•
for one and a half seconds
i couldn't separate
what I saw, with what I heard!

Then I realized that
the sounds of the city are not so different from the sounds
that each of us hears inside.

Two worlds aligned
and introduced•
in the same head.
85 — m

writings.title: Ostridge
writings.body:
Supermarket. Checkout queue. 
Right in front of me is a lady.
He had a few things.

When it was time for her to pay, I approached her to leave my things at the checkout, so I heard her address the cashier:
'Oh, I almost forgot. Bring me a pack of cigarettes (of a brand) from the window. But not to have a picture of blood and stuff.'

From the background you can hear the cashier:
"There's a package left and there's a child with cancer on it, do you want it?"
'Yeah, all right, bring it.'

Duh! 
In other news, according to Pliny the Elder, ostriches hide their heads in the sand when they see an enemy. 
And we humans laughabout it.
Because we humans know. 

85 — m

writings.title: Coincidences
writings.body:
I am walking up Martiou street with my guitar.
In my headphones playing on loop since this morning
"I loοοοve you, I love youuu because you're beauuutifuul"
I am on the right side of the street
and my eye catches a gentleman (eighty-something)
sitting on a piece of cardboard, on the opposite sidewalk, playing his violin and singing.
In my hurry I think "let me listen to what this man has to say, after all what I'm listening to I've already heard about 7 times"
I take off my headphones;
"I loοοove youuu and I love theee whole wooorld"
A supernatural force convinced me in fractions of a second that this coincidence truly had something to tell me.
He sees me with the guitar from across the street and gestured for me to come closer.
-I wish I had change to leave for you, but I have nothing. Can I get you something to eat, or drink?
-My boy, I saw you with the guitar and you made me happy, I am 85 years old and I have three sons who now live in Cyprus, all musicians - they do their regular jobs but they also have music. Ever since they were small children I told them to keep music in their heart and never let it go. I've played in venues, officially, unofficially, with money and without. The most important thing to remember is to have your instrument express you and for you to be able to enjoy yourself. Nothing else matters, and I'm telling you this as an 85-year-old whose children are away and whose wife passed away.
I brought him a frappe that he wanted. I feel grateful that I listened to the music inside me, just like Mr. S. did.
Trust and let the music inside you show you the way, in the simplest everyday things.
It is not a coincidence, it is not supernatural.
It is us.

y.f.

writings.title: How embarrassing!
One tooth
writings.body:
Nine o'clock in the morning, I sit on a bench in Venizelou Square (the Lions we call Heraklion) and wait patiently, with a coffee in hand, for the employee of the next photo shop to finish with my service. 
He hadn't caught my eye. A gentleman of about 60 years old, medium height, slender, with fisherman's hair emerges from my left like a tornado: 
'Come on, do we need anything?' This gentleman seemed willing to help with whatever work he was assigned. So, because he was used to it. Like a masterpiece. No one ever answered him, he generously handed out greetings to passers-by.
So, because he was used to it.
'Good morning, good job, what are we doing?'
Good morning.
"Good morning and have a good week"
Good morning. 
No response. Frankly speaking, I was sad. I tried to be discreet and with the edge of my eye I saw him, standing there and swayed by his enthusiasm like a pole, leaning on the back wall skeptically, with his hand on his chin and with his eyes going back and forth in the world that was passing by. At one moment, one of his elders, who must have been often passing by this place, saw him:
"Well done!" he said with the characteristic Cretan bravado.
He was stunned again and a smile flashed, bringing out the whole one tooth that had remained in his mouth!
A tooth.
And yet his smile was the most sincere I've ever seen.
A tooth.
And yet, he knows how to say good morning, selflessly.
A tooth.
And yet, he knows how to share his magic with those around him.
Imagine how much magic he would emit if he had all his teeth. 
I felt grateful to have all my teeth. I will make the most of it!
Like him, with what's left of him.

85 — m

writings.title: The paradox of global poverty
writings.body:
Conversation between an airplane passenger
and an employee
at the airport security check:

-Sir, you cannot go through here (pointing to an empty lane leading to an empty x-ray).
You must go through there (pointing to a crowded path).
-But the lane is empty here.
-Yes, but this is the fast lane. For passengers who have paid.
-But no one is coming, we will facilitate the flow.
-That is the point of the fast lane.
Unintentionally, the employee uttered a great truth.
And right there I realized that the fast lane is a service with, theoretically, a huge risk.
The possibility that no one uses the fast lane
and everyone goes through the other entrances
or the possibility that everyone goes to the fast lane,
both carry the risk of it losing its meaning.
Because the "service" - hot air offered as a privilege,
when it becomes a privilege for everyone, then it is one no longer.
It's not the fast lane's fault,
it's the privileges we think we are granted.
It's all a matter of balance.
For a fast lane to exist,
no company wants all of its passengers to afford it.
Paradoxical ( ; )

y.f.

writings.title: Hair
writings.body:
Taking the last little shower of the year,
a conversation I had
this year with a hairdresser came to mind:
I am sitting in the familiar chair,
in front of the mirror,
he looks at me through the mirror,
gives me a pat-pat on the shoulder
and tells me the epic line "you're right-handed, aren't you".
Astonished and at the same time suspicious
that he played the odds,
I answer him "yes, but why?".
With the familiar smirk as if saying "I know",
he tells me "the little bald spot is growing more on the right than on the left".
LITTLE BALD SPOT?!
Right there I started talking to him about heredity,
genes,
hair gel I used to put on back in the day,
and other such things.
He interrupted me, saying the following:
"Your right hand, Yiorghi,
is your strongest.
With it you comb your hair back (I had long hair back then).
The hair is weaker than your hand and gives in.
Don't forget to respect the weak."
To take care of
our weak parts,
with gentleness.
To comb them
respecting their vulnerabilities;
no matter how well they hide them.

y.f.
